text:
sanjeev: Quick check: RFC asked for splitting control plane for private/VPC customers. For cost reasons we planned to keep a shared egress relay for small tenants to avoid burning /27s. Question: are we okay delegating the auth boundary to the tenant connector (agent) instead of terminating at a CP proxy? Main risks I see: cert churn, connector transient loss, and NAT IP exhaustion on shared-relay.

marie: Sounds reasonable in principle. We need strict semantics for fallback when a tenant connector becomes unreachable. Who owns retry/backoff / circuit-breaker — CP or tenant agent?

alan: My take: CP should own retries/idempotent control-plane retries. For data-plane egress (customer workload out to internet or model store) we delegate primary routing to tenant sidecar/connector. Fallback semantics: if connector reports `egress_down` or fails health, CP will route that tenant to shared-relay with per-tenant tag.

prashant: Cost reminder: shared-relay uses an SNAT pool => IPs are scarce/expensive. If we route many tenants to shared-relay during outages we can blow past our IP allocations and SRE quotas. We should define billing: either platform absorbs occasional fallback or we bill tenants per allocated fallback IP if they opt out of dedicated egress. Need product callout.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out cp-split v2 to canary (us-west-2) — 3 instances. No errors in logs in last 2h.

sophie: Operationally we need a structured fallback reason surface in telemetry. Proposed reason-codes: connector-unreachable, cert-mismatch, quota-exceeded, ip-exhaustion, admin-forced. That will let SREs and customers filter alert blasts.

rachael: Proposal for minimal handshake change: connector advertises `egress_preference: "local" | "relay"`. CP attempts local route if connector says local. On failing local route, CP switches to `shared-relay` and emits fallback reason. Add a small health endpoint `/v1/egress_status` on the connector returning status + last_error. Example health payload (for ops only):

```
{
  "egress": "local",
  "status": "degraded",
  "last_error": "connectivity: timed out to nat-gw",
  "fallback_count": 3
}
```

marie: Also need a TLS cert rotation verification for shared-relay trust. Avoid long-lived bootstrap tokens for connectors. We should standardize a short-lived client cert + OIDC bootstrap flow.

alan: For rollout: start with a very small canary (0.5% tenants) using shared-relay fallback, monitor error codes and p99 latency, then scale. Need a kill-switch in case SNAT pool pressure spikes.

sanjeev: Action items: prashant update billing note (fallback IP charging), sophie add fallback codes to telemetry schema, rachael draft handshake + health endpoint patch, alan write canary rollout + kill-switch runbook. I'll sync with Security on cert rotation. @here — objections by EOD otherwise we'll spin a spike branch and schedule a short demo next week :thumbsup:
